strings.en:
{09:0f}{0b:06}The Anoian Faith and Angels

Since ancient times, people have projected the
forces of nature upon their gods. Lightning,
sunlight, moonlight, darkness, the earth that
brings forth crops, the sea, the wind, the
motions of the stars, the seasons, death,
sickness... The ancients furnished many gods to
preside over these. Before the birth of the
Anoian faith, the world was filled with
thousands of gods. But the Anoian faith
concentrated in the Two Supreme Gods, Zemen
and Zeweak, the powers and authority that
many gods had divided among themselves, and
denied the existence of any god but the Two
Supreme Gods. As a result, these Two Supreme
Gods came to hold an immense power such as
no god had ever held.

However, because so much power was
concentrated in the Two Supreme Gods, and
because of the ban on idolatry besides, Zemen
and Zeweak became highly abstract beings. And
they lost even the human warmth and
approachability that the old gods had
possessed.

In every age, the people look to God for readily
understood miracles and for tangible blessings
such as rich harvests and the healing of
sickness. And in spreading the Anoian faith,
too, the Two Supreme Gods proved far too
abstract and hard to grasp for people used to
polytheism.

So, to solve this problem, the Anoian Church
recast the native gods of the north, east and
west as beings called "angels", and entrusted
the task of granting blessings and miracles to
the "angels", the "Thirteen Saints" and the
"other saints".

"Angels" are creatures made by the Two
Supreme Gods to mediate and form a bridge
between God and humankind... Thus does the
Church explain the existence of angels. If
angels are not equals of the Two Supreme
Gods but beings created by them, the standing
of the Two Supreme Gods, Zemen and Zeweak,
is not shaken in the least.

Further, in the Scriptures, the Prophet Anoia
and the Thirteen Saints forbade enshrining
images of God, but did not forbid making images
of angels and Saints... Therefore, there is no
problem whatever in adorning a church with
images of angels...

And so was born the easily understood,
approachable guardian called an "angel".

-Addendum 1-

The tale of angels fighting to cast the Devil
out of God's paradise was created fully two
thousand years after the founding of the
Anoian faith. Before then, angels had no role
but to carry God's word to the people, but as
the Holy See's power grew, so did their role as
guardians of God and of the Anoian faith.

-Addendum 2-

The Krasdar Eastern Orthodox Church denies
the existence of angels, and even faith in the
Prophet Anoia and the Holy Mother. The
Eastern Orthodox Church recognizes no faith
but in Zemen and Zeweak. And it forbids
adorning a church with any image at all.{0b:07}

strings.jp: 教会
strings.read: 教会
strings.en: The Church
strings.tl: The Church

strings.jp:
{09:0f}{0b:06}教会

 教会とは本来、ゼメンとゼウェアクの二至高
神と神の御子アノイアに対して人々が信仰を誓
う場所であり、司祭や司教、教皇などの教会の
聖職者達は、神の教えを人々に説き、神と人々
との架け橋をつくる役割を持っていた。
 しかし、5千年の間に教会も変わってきた。
貧しい民衆の中には、いまだ敬虔な信仰を持ち
続けている人々の方が多いだろうが、神に仕え
るべき聖職者で神の存在を信じている者など、
ほとんどいないのではないだろうか。

 教会内部の退廃は激しく、教義は歪曲され、
教会の儀式も形骸化している。司祭達は、民衆
に地獄や天罰の恐怖のみを説き、地獄に堕ちた
くなければと民衆に規定外の税を要求し、都市
部では高額の免罪符を発行し続けた。教会の最
高権力者である教皇は、まるで国王のように振
る舞い、酒と女に溺れているという。

 このような教会に対して、民衆が何も思わな
いわけはなかった。アスロイトのある大司教領
内で発生した農民の武装蜂起で代表者達は「ア
ノイア教は信じるがアノイア教会は信じない」
と宣誓し、多くの人々の賛同を得た。
 回帰運動(アノイア教を本来の姿に戻そうと
いう運動)も各地でおこっていたが、教会はそ
れらに対して、その国の政府と組み容赦ない弾
圧を加えた。民衆は、国王と教会の2つの支配
者に苦しめられていたのである。{0b:07}

strings.en:
{09:0f}{0b:06}The Church

The Church was originally a place where people
swore their faith to the Two Supreme Gods,
Zemen and Zeweak, and to Anoia, Child of God,
and its clergy, the priests, bishops and Pope,
had the role of preaching God's teachings to
the people and building a bridge between God
and the people. But over five thousand years
the Church has changed. Among the poor,
those who keep a devout faith are surely still
the majority, but among the clergy who ought
to serve God, hardly any, I suspect, believe
that God exists.

Decadence within the Church is severe:
doctrine is distorted, and its rites are hollow
forms. Priests preach to the people only the
terror of hell and divine punishment, demand
taxes beyond those prescribed from any who
wish not to fall into hell, and in the cities have
gone on issuing costly indulgences. The Pope,
the highest authority of the Church, is said to
behave like a king and to drown in wine and
women.

The people could hardly think nothing of such a
Church. In an armed peasant uprising that broke
out in an archbishop's domain in Asroit, the
leaders swore, "We believe in the Anoian faith,
but not in the Anoian Church", and won the
support of many. Return movements
(movements to restore the Anoian faith to its
original form) also arose in various places, but
the Church, joining with each country's
government, suppressed them without mercy.
The people were suffering under two rulers,
king and Church.{0b:07}
strings.tl:
The Church

The Church was originally a place where people swore their faith to the Two Supreme Gods, Zemen and Zeweak, and to Anoia, Child of God, and its clergy, the priests, bishops and Pope, had the role of preaching God's teachings to the people and building a bridge between God and the people. But over five thousand years the Church has changed. Among the poor, those who keep a devout faith are surely still the majority, but among the clergy who ought to serve God, hardly any, I suspect, believe that God exists.

Decadence within the Church is severe: doctrine is distorted, and its rites are hollow forms. Priests preach to the people only the terror of hell and divine punishment, demand taxes beyond those prescribed from any who wish not to fall into hell, and in the cities have gone on issuing costly indulgences. The Pope, the highest authority of the Church, is said to behave like a king and to drown in wine and women.

The people could hardly think nothing of such a Church. In an armed peasant uprising that broke out in an archbishop's domain in Asroit, the leaders swore, "We believe in the Anoian faith, but not in the Anoian Church", and won the support of many. Return movements (movements to restore the Anoian faith to its original form) also arose in various places, but the Church, joining with each country's government, suppressed them without mercy. The people were suffering under two rulers, king and Church.

strings.en:
{09:0f}{0b:06}The Anoian Calendar

The calendar of the Anoian faith is a classical
lunar calendar, with 30 days to a month. A year
is therefore 360 days. For recording years, it
is common to use the "Anoian calendar",
counted from the year the Anoian faith was
born (that is, the year the Prophet Anoia
received God's revelation). Incidentally, there
are many theories that the faith was born
several years before that. Some even hold the
absurd theory that it was as much as five
thousand years earlier.{0b:07}

Incidentally, there are many theories that the faith was born several years before that. Some even hold the absurd theory that it was as much as five thousand years earlier.

strings.jp:
{09:0f}{0b:06}預言者と十三聖者

 預言者{03}アノイア{02}がいなければ世界最大の宗教
{03}アノイア教{02}は存在しなかった。人間の中で最も
神に近づいた存在、それが{03}アノイア{02}である。

 しかしながら預言者{03}アノイア{02}の正確な資料は、
実は何も残っていない。
 悪魔の誘惑に打ち勝ちこれを遠ざけた、木の
葉を{03}パン{02}に変え飢えた人々を救った、悪魔に操
られた友人を救うために自らの命を差しだした、
生まれてすぐに聖なる言葉を発した、などの預
言者{03}アノイア{02}に関する有名な逸話は全て後世つ
くられたもので、歴史ではなく伝承にすぎない
のである。しかも、その伝承を受け継いだのは
{03}アノイア教徒{02}で、これらの伝承が客観的な資料

{09:0f}{0b:06}The Prophet and the Thirteen Saints

Without the Prophet Anoia, the Anoian faith,
the largest religion in the world, would not exist.
The one among humans who came closest to
God: that is Anoia.

And yet no accurate record of the Prophet
Anoia in fact survives. He overcame the Devil's
temptation and drove it away; he turned leaves
into bread and saved the starving; he gave his
own life to save a friend controlled by the
Devil; he spoke holy words right after he was
born: these famous anecdotes of the Prophet
Anoia were all created by later generations, and
are mere tradition, not history. What is more, it
was Anoian believers who handed down those
traditions, so I doubt they can serve as
objective sources.

Anoia received God's revelation at 18 (some say
17) and met a tragic death as the Child of God
at 19. His time as Prophet was overwhelmingly
brief, which is partly why, after five thousand
years, there is no telling what philosophy this
man held (some say Anoia was a woman), or how
he came to hold it.

The "Scriptures", which set out the ideals and
thought of the Prophet Anoia, are written
entirely as the Thirteen Saints' recollections:
"Anoia said thus at that time." Taking a cynical
view, one could even say that the Thirteen
Saints created a fictional person called Anoia
and cast that person as savior and Prophet. (A
rather absurd view, admittedly.)

Unlike Anoia, the Thirteen Saints are
remembered in detailed traditions. While Anoia
never left Shiomen, the Thirteen Saints spent
decades traveling and preaching through many
lands, so they remain in the records even of
those who persecuted the Anoian faith.

Just as the Anoian faith would not exist
without Anoia, without the Thirteen Saints the
faith whose seed Anoia sowed would never have
grown into so great a tree. Without the First
Saint Avadail's establishment of the Church
system, the mission to Remus by the Second
Saint Barkail and the Third Saint Gambial, and
the compiling of the systematized Scriptures by
the Twelfth Saint Hanrial and the last Saint
Welkail, the Anoian faith might have ended as a
mere local religion.{0b:07}
strings.tl:
The Prophet and the Thirteen Saints

Without the Prophet Anoia, the Anoian faith, the largest religion in the world, would not exist. The one among humans who came closest to God: that is Anoia.

And yet no accurate record of the Prophet Anoia in fact survives. He overcame the Devil's temptation and drove it away; he turned leaves into bread and saved the starving; he gave his own life to save a friend controlled by the Devil; he spoke holy words right after he was born: these famous anecdotes of the Prophet Anoia were all created by later generations, and are mere tradition, not history. What is more, it was Anoian believers who handed down those traditions, so I doubt they can serve as objective sources.

Anoia received God's revelation at 18 (some say 17) and met a tragic death as the Child of God at 19. His time as Prophet was overwhelmingly brief, which is partly why, after five thousand years, there is no telling what philosophy this man held (some say Anoia was a woman), or how he came to hold it.

The "Scriptures", which set out the ideals and thought of the Prophet Anoia, are written entirely as the Thirteen Saints' recollections: "Anoia said thus at that time." Taking a cynical view, one could even say that the Thirteen Saints created a fictional person called Anoia and cast that person as savior and Prophet. (A rather absurd view, admittedly.)

Unlike Anoia, the Thirteen Saints are remembered in detailed traditions. While Anoia never left Shiomen, the Thirteen Saints spent decades traveling and preaching through many lands, so they remain in the records even of those who persecuted the Anoian faith.

Just as the Anoian faith would not exist without Anoia, without the Thirteen Saints the faith whose seed Anoia sowed would never have grown into so great a tree. Without the First Saint Avadail's establishment of the Church system, the mission to Remus by the Second Saint Barkail and the Third Saint Gambial, and the compiling of the systematized Scriptures by the Twelfth Saint Hanrial and the last Saint Welkail, the Anoian faith might have ended as a mere local religion.
